description: Search the machine-read text of every archive this server reads that holds any, at the same time, and get one list of where a phrase was printed. The archives behind this tool hold different material, so the list is additive: it is the places a phrase appears in each corpus, put together, rather than the same question answered twice. 'per_source' names what each corpus is. A match carries 'page_number', which is a real leaf on an archive whose index holds one and null on an archive whose index holds none. That null is the index having no leaf, never a page this server dropped, and no page is ever invented. A match also carries 'excerpt_kind'. 'passage' is the text around the words that matched. 'page_opening' is the start of the page, sent because the machine-read text that came back stops before the searched words appear, so it does not carry the match. The notes say how many excerpts are openings. Every count is that archive's own and counts something of its own: documents in one place, leaves in another. They are never added together, and there is no total across archives. Rows are interleaved one archive at a time. Nothing ranks them against each other and nothing orders them by date, because a year is measured on different things in each archive. Matches whose excerpt carries the searched words are placed before matches whose excerpt is a 'page_opening' and carries them nowhere. That rests on what each row states about its own excerpt rather than on any score, no match is ever dropped for it, and the interleaving holds inside each of the two groups. The archives read the words given in different ways, and 'per_source' says which each one does. An index that answers only where every word appears returns nothing for a question written as a sentence, even on a work it holds several copies of; an index that scores the words instead answers such a question with the pages it ranks highest, which can carry only some of them. Either way it is the words: a character that is neither a letter nor a digit is no word to an index, and 'non_word_characters' lists any the query carried. Shorter and differently spelled wordings are therefore derived from the query and asked for their union, which costs nothing extra when the words as asked already answer. Every wording sent is named in 'per_source' with what it returned, every match carries the wording that returned it in 'found_by_query', and 'fan_out' turns the derivation off. Use search_items for a work by its title, its creator or its subject: this tool reads the text on the pages and knows nothing of a catalogue, so a title given here finds every book that happens to mention it and misses the book itself. Answers take several seconds, because one of the archives publishes a request ceiling this server keeps to. A slow answer is the pacing, not a stall.

fan_out.description: Whether to derive shorter and differently spelled wordings from the query and ask each archive for the union of what they return. A question written as a sentence returns nothing where every word given has to appear, and the rows an index scores highest where it does not. An archive is asked a derived wording only when the words as asked did not return as many rows as 'limit', so a query that works costs one request. Set false to send exactly the words given. 'per_source' names every wording, sent or not, and each match names the one that returned it.

limit.description: Matches to take from each archive, so one archive cannot fill the whole list. The text block shows about six matches; the rest of what comes back is in the structured output.

max_excerpt_chars.description: Budget for one passage. Read it together with 'max_excerpts_per_match': the size of the answer is the product of the two, the limit, and the number of archives.

max_excerpts_per_match.description: Passages to keep per match. A long work matches in several places, and the later ones rarely say anything the first did not.

page.description: Which page of matches, from 1. Each archive is paged separately.

query.description: Words, or a phrase in double quotes such as '"call me ishmael"'.

sources.description: Archives to ask, by id. Left out, every archive that reads machine-read text is asked, which is the point of this tool.

name: search_inside

excerpt_kinds.description: How many excerpts here are of each kind.

page_opening.description: Excerpts that are the opening of a page and do not carry the match.

passage.description: Excerpts that carry the words that matched.

hit_count.description: Matches in this answer, across every archive. It is a count of what came back, never a total of what exists.

excerpt_kind.description: 'passage' means the text around the words that matched. 'page_opening' means the start of the page, sent because the machine-read text that came back with this row stops before the searched words appear. A page_opening does not carry the match.

excerpts.description: Machine-read text, all of one kind for this match.

found_by_derivation.description: How that wording was arrived at from the question, in words.

found_by_query.description: The wording this archive was given that returned this row. It is the query as you wrote it unless a further wording was derived, in which case the row answers that wording's words and not the rest of the question.

id.description: Pass this to get_item. It names its archive, so nothing is guessed.

identifier.description: The archive's own identifier, without the prefix.

inside_container.description: True when the passage comes from a document bundled inside the record, in which case the title, creator and year above describe the container rather than the text that matched.

matched_file.description: The document the passage sits in, when the record bundles several. Null when the record is the document.

page_number.description: The leaf the passage sits on. Null on an archive whose full-text index holds no leaf number: read 'publishes_page_number' in 'per_source' to tell that from a row where a leaf simply was not given. Never invent one.

publication.description: The newspaper the page belongs to, where there is one.

published_on.description: Date of the issue, as published, on a corpus dated by issue.

source_url.description: The page itself. Show this when citing the match.

year.description: What this archive calls a year. The archives measure it on different things, so 'per_source' says what it means on each and no order is imposed across them.

non_word_characters.description: Characters in the query that are neither letters nor digits. These indexes answer on words, so a match here can carry none of them, and 'requires_every_word' covers the words that were given rather than these.

order.description: How the list was built, in words.

absent_because.description: Why this archive was left out. Null unless the status is absent.

attribution.description: What to say when repeating what this archive contributed, as this archive states it for this answer. An archive whose licence asks for the date its metadata was retrieved carries that date here. Null on an archive that was never asked.

cached.description: Served from this server's short-lived in-memory cache.

corpus.description: What body of material this archive's full-text index reads. Null where this answer did not read it.

count.description: Rows this archive contributed to the answer.

error.description: Why this archive did not answer. Null when it did.

filters_dropped.description: Narrowings you asked for that this archive never received, because its catalogue cannot apply them. Its rows were not narrowed by them, and a row from it that happens to satisfy one is a coincidence rather than a filter. Empty when it received every narrowing asked for.

because.description: Why this archive never received it.

filter.description: The narrowing, named as the argument that carries it.

media_type_asked.description: The name this archive was asked to look under, in its own vocabulary. Null where it searches every kind at once.

more_on_this_archive.description: Whether this archive says it holds matches beyond the page just read. Raise 'page' to read them. Null where it states no total, and on an archive that was never asked.

ordered_on.description: What this archive ordered its own rows on. No order runs across archives.

publishes_page_number.description: Whether this archive's full-text index holds a leaf number. False makes every 'page_number' from it null by nature.

queries.description: Every wording derived for this archive, in the order they were tried, with what each one returned and why any was withheld. Retyping one of them reproduces its rows by hand. Empty on a call that carries no query.

added.description: Rows this wording contributed that an earlier one had not already returned. Null when it was not sent, or did not answer.

count.description: Rows the archive returned for this wording. Zero is that wording finding nothing, which is a statement about the wording. Null when it was not sent, or did not answer.

derivation.description: How this wording was arrived at from the question, in words.

error.description: Why this wording did not answer. Null when it did, or was never sent.

not_run_because.description: Why it was withheld. Null when it was sent.

query.description: The words this archive was given, exactly as they were sent.

ran.description: Whether it was sent. False means it was derived and withheld.

reported_total.description: What this archive said it saw. Null when it states no number at all.

reported_total_means.description: What 'reported_total' counts on this archive. The archives count different things and these numbers are never added together.

requires_every_word.description: Whether the index this answer put the words to answers only where every word given appears. It covers the words: a character that is neither a letter nor a digit is not a word to an index, and those are listed in 'non_word_characters' instead. False means the index ranks the words and answers with what it scores highest, so one of its rows can carry only some of them. Null on an archive that was not asked.

row_describes.description: What one row from this archive is: a copy it holds, a record in a catalogue, or a work as an entity whose editions are records of their own. Rows carry the same fields and describe different kinds of thing.

searches_on.description: The fields this archive matched the query against. The archives read different ones, so the same words are not the same question everywhere, and a name given to an index over titles alone comes back as the works written about that person.

skipped.description: Rows this archive sent in a shape the server could not read, and left out of this answer. Always a count, so it reads the same way on every answer. Rows served out of a cache were counted the same way when they were first read, and 'cached' marks an answer whose count can be short of a drop nobody kept a record of.

stage.description: Which moment this report is about: the search that looks for records, or the read that opens one. Null on an archive that was never asked. A search that did not answer and a search that answered before a read failed are different statements.

status.description: 'answered' means it replied. 'failed' means it was asked and did not. 'absent' means it was never asked, and 'absent_because' says why.

year_means.description: What a 'year' on this archive's rows was measured on.

queries_run.description: Requests this server sent for this answer, counting every wording on every archive. Each archive's own wordings are in 'per_source'.

title: Find a phrase in the scanned text of every archive
